title: Strategic alignment handoff and initiative origami
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: As we scale product and platform work into Q2, teams report repeated rework and unclear acceptance criteria when initiatives transition from strategy -> tactical roadmap. Cross-functional dependencies are identified late and cause scope churn during cycle planning.

Goal: Create a repeatable 'handoff' pattern and lightweight artifact set ("initiative packet") plus a rotating alignment ritual so company-level OKRs map cleanly to team deliverables, dependencies are surfaced earlier, and product/eng/design can commit to sprintable scopes with fewer mid-cycle pivots.

Scope: Define the initiative packet template, run a 3-week pilot with Platform, Console, and Dedicated teams, create a triage rotation and 30/60/90 rollout gates, and add a minimal telemetry rubric to measure OKR->deliverable fidelity. Deliverables include: initiative packet template (Confluence), handoff checklist, triage rotation schedule, pilot retro, and three example initiative packets for Platform infra, Runtime performance, and Console UX.

Out of scope: Replacing existing OKR process entirely, making changes to compensation goals, or reworking team-level sprint cadence.

Success metrics: 50% reduction in mid-cycle scope changes for pilot teams, >80% initiative packets marked "ready for sprint" by gate 2, and 1 exported dependency dashboard (Confluence/Notion) showing cross-team blockers resolved <14 days on average.
acceptance_criteria: Initiative packet template published in Confluence with fields: owner, hypothesis, success metrics, acceptance criteria, rollout gates, dependency register, risk/tradeoffs, minimal implementation plan.
Triage rotation schedule published and staffed for next three cycles (owner + backup per week).
Pilot run completed with Platform, Console, Dedicated; retro captured and action items prioritized.
Three example initiative packets created and reviewed by respective PM + Eng + Design leads.
Dependency dashboard (Notion page) seeded with all pilot dependencies and linked issues (Linear/GitHub) for visibility.
